Overview of the 2022 WHO Classification of Paragangliomas and Pheochromocytomas. Endocrine Pathology 2022;33(1):90-114, PMID 35285002 -- full text read 16 Sep 2026 -- and the WHO Paediatric Tumours volume, both 2022) per build contract instruction (Group 4 build contract, pre-context table). NOTE the edition nuance recorded at contract §10.1: the fixed rule that all PPGLs (paragangliomas and pheochromocytomas) are behaviour-3 neoplasms with variable metastatic potential was already settled in the 4th edition, 2017, not the 5th: "Prior to the 2017 WHO classification (also known the 4th edition), PPGLs... were accompanied by the adjectives 'benign' or 'malignant'.... As a result, all PPGLs have been considered as malignant neoplasms with variable metastatic potential." (Mete 2022, p. 100). "WHO 2022" here names the edition that classifies and names the individual entities on this stem, not the edition that first fixed the behaviour. Mete 2022 never states an ICD-O code anywhere in the paper (contract §10.1) -- it corroborates that a current WHO entity lives on the stem; icdo32.sqlite states the number. IHC panel per Mete 2022 (pp. 96-106, full text read 16 Sep 2026): synaptophysin and chromogranin A are the general neuroendocrine markers the WHO panel recommends; GATA3 is the specific marker that separates a paraganglioma/pheochromocytoma from a neuroblastic tumour at the same site (build contract §5.1); cytokeratin is negative in both families and separates neither from the other, only both from a well-differentiated neuroendocrine tumour. PHOX2B is not listed here: Mete 2022 discusses PHOX2B only under the neuroblastoma differential (p. 108), never as a paraganglioma/pheochromocytoma marker, and PHOX2B does not separate neuroblastoma from pheochromocytoma/paraganglioma -- both are PHOX2B positive (contract §5.1, §10.1). A branch citing PHOX2B for this family must cite Manethova 2023, not WHO. 8683 Gangliocytic paraganglioma is NOT built in this file (build contract §0.2): icdo32.sqlite carries it only at behaviour /0, and ICCC-3 Group IV declares behaviour 3 only, so there is no 8683/3 to author. Independently, Mete 2022 (p. 94) confirms WHO 2022 renamed the entity "composite gangliocytoma/neuroma and neuroendocrine tumor (CoGNET)", walking it out of the paraganglioma family entirely -- both legs of the two-source test agree it is removed. 8683 appears nowhere in this file as a morphology_code or alias target; it may only be an alias input resolving to a terminal that explains why it cannot be coded here and refers the case to the registrar. Whether WHO 2022 states an ICD-O code for CoGNET is unknown -- only the Mete 2022 abstract carries the CoGNET quote with no page number; the full text (p. 94) confirms it but still states no code.

morphology_entries.imaging_features: Elevated plasma free metanephrines or 24-hour urinary fractionated metanephrines, plus catecholamines and chromogranin A, together with an imaging-demonstrated adrenal (or, for the extra-adrenal presentation, paraspinal/retroperitoneal) mass at a site consistent with pheochromocytoma. Visser MJ, et al. key-points summary, Table 4 (p. 06), names this constellation -- catecholamines and chromogranin A -- as sufficient for coding 8700/3 with no tissue diagnosis, ENCR basis of diagnosis 4. Rule 6 (p. 05): basis 4 never stands alone -- the biochemical marker must accompany a clinical diagnosis or a clinical investigation (here, the imaging finding) showing cancer, not stand alone as a laboratory abnormality.

DIVERGENCE, recorded not acted on (build contract §4.2): Visser's own Table 4 (p. 06) places pheochromocytoma in Group XI, not Group IV. ICCC-2017 is Layer 1 and governs, and ICCC-2017 puts 8700 in IVb -- the routing does not change. One of the two Visser Table 4 rows this group owns (with 9500): catecholamines and chromogranin A plus imaging is a valid basis-4, no-tissue diagnosis for this code alone. COMPOSITE PPGL (composite paraganglioma/pheochromocytoma): icdo32.sqlite carries "Composite pheochromocytoma" as a Related term on this stem. Mete 2022 (p. 106) reports composite PPGL is about 75% pheochromocytoma-with-ganglioneuroma and about 10% each with neuroblastoma or ganglioneuroblastoma, described in adults ("fourth to fifth decade", p. 106). A composite case's ganglioneuroma component must not be routed to the D1 behaviour_exclusion terminal (build contract §3, §6 D1) -- the composite lesion as a whole stays coded to its pheochromocytoma or paraganglioma stem, not split into an excluded benign component plus a separate malignant one. Mete 2022's own abstract writes "composite paraganglioma" while the body always writes "composite PPGL" or "composite pheochromocytoma" -- an inconsistency in the source, recorded so nobody reconciles it silently (contract §10.1).

RULING D1 (build contract §2.1, §3, §6): 9490/0 is Ganglioneuroma, benign -- the fully matured end of the neuroblastic spectrum -- and is NOT authored in this file. ICCC-3 Group IV admits behaviour 3 only, so a ganglioneuroma is not a registrable Group IV cancer. This is the group's central trap: a tree that resolves "Schwannian stroma-dominant, maturing or mature" to the 9490 stem without checking behaviour would silently emit 9490/3 Ganglioneuroblastoma for a benign tumour. The behaviour_exclusion field (contract §3, ratified by the registrar) is how the tree (Tasks 4-6) must handle this -- a branch or terminal carrying it emits no morphology_code, states the lesion is 9490/0 Ganglioneuroma, benign, and refers the decision to the registrar. Precedent: Group 3 left 8000/6 and 8000/9 unauthored for the same reason. The REDCap option file lists "Ganglioneuroma" as if it were a 9490 option string -- it is not; it is 9490/0 and is not built here (build contract §0.3). CNS NOTE (build contract §0.6): icdo32.sqlite carries synonym or related terms tying this stem to the central nervous system -- yet ICCC-3 places this code in Group IVa at every site, including the CNS, and Group III does not claim it. This reads wrong to a reviewer who expects a CNS-sited tumour to route to Group III; it is not an error, it is how ICCC-3 states the group. Do not "fix" it by adding a CNS carve-out. (Related term here is "CNS ganglioneuroblastoma".) Falls back to 9500. IHC panel per Mete 2022 (p. 108) and the sympathoadrenal differential (build contract §5.1): PHOX2B, synaptophysin and chromogranin positive; cytokeratin negative. PHOX2B does NOT separate this from pheochromocytoma/paraganglioma -- both families are PHOX2B positive; GATA3 and the sustentacular S100/SOX10 pattern are what separate them (contract §5.1, §10.1) -- do not add GATA3 to this entry's required panel, it is a paraganglioma/pheochromocytoma marker, not a neuroblastic one. Evidence: Shimada 1999 and Peuchmaur 2003 (the International Neuroblastoma Pathology Committee, INPC, classification), Monclair 2009 and Ambros 2005/2009 (the International Neuroblastoma Risk Group, INRG) -- the group's best-evidenced family, corroborated a second time by Mete 2022 Table 1 (p. 108), which independently reproduces the full INPC classification (undifferentiated, poorly differentiated, differentiating; intermixed, nodular; maturing, mature) attributed to Shimada 1999. who_version recorded WHO 2022 per the Mete 2022 / WHO Paediatric Tumours convergence; the underlying INPC criteria that actually separate this code from 9500 and from 9490/0 are Shimada 1999, predating either 2022 document.

morphology_entries.imaging_features: Elevated urinary homovanillic acid (HVA) and vanillylmandelic acid (VMA), together with an imaging-demonstrated mass at a site typical of a neuroblastic primary (adrenal, paraspinal/retroperitoneal, posterior mediastinal, or elsewhere along the sympathetic chain) consistent with neuroblastoma. Visser MJ, et al. key-points summary, Table 4 (p. 06), names this constellation -- urinary HVA and VMA -- as sufficient for coding 9500/3 with no tissue diagnosis, ENCR basis of diagnosis 4, not basis 2. Rule 6 (p. 05): basis 4 never stands alone -- the biochemical marker must accompany a clinical diagnosis or a clinical investigation (the imaging finding) showing cancer, not stand alone as a laboratory abnormality.

decision_trees.tree_label: Sympathoadrenal axis — adrenal gland, peripheral nerve and autonomic nervous system, retroperitoneum and mediastinum (C74.0, C74.1, C74.9, C47.0–C47.9, C48.0, C48.2, C48.8, C38.1–C38.3)

nodes.question: Sympathoadrenal-region mass — adrenal gland (C74.0, C74.1, C74.9), peripheral nerve or autonomic nervous system (C47.0–C47.9), retroperitoneum (C48.0, C48.2, C48.8), or mediastinum (C38.1–C38.3). What is actually in this patient's file, and was the specimen adequate for diagnosis?
nodes.hint: Pick the highest evidence tier present. This compartment holds two biologically distinct tumour families — the neuroblastic spectrum (neuroblastoma, ganglioneuroblastoma, ganglioneuroma) and the paraganglioma/pheochromocytoma family — plus, at the adrenal gland specifically, an epithelial differential (adrenocortical carcinoma). Record adequacy honestly: an uninterpretable specimen is not a negative one.
nodes.coding_note: ENCR basis of diagnosis is computed as the highest of codes 1-8 (0 and 9 override). ihc_counts_as 7, methylation_counts_as 8 are declared on the tree object (build contract §4.2). Only 9500/3 and 8700/3 may be assigned on imaging alone, at basis 4, and only with a biochemical marker AND the imaging finding together (Visser Rule 6, p.05) — never on imaging alone. Every other code in this tree requires tissue.

options.label: Referral letter or clinical note only — no imaging report, no laboratory result and no pathology report
Imaging report (CT/MRI) with a biochemical or catecholamine work-up documented — no tissue and no cytology
Fine-needle aspiration or core-needle cytology only — no excisional or incisional biopsy report is in the file
Definitive histology report — no immunohistochemistry performed or reported

A specimen was taken but the report says it is inadequate, non-diagnostic, or crush artefact only

options.reason: The lesion was reviewed and is not a neoplasm. Adrenal haemorrhage in a neonate, extramedullary haematopoiesis, and other non-neoplastic causes of a sympathoadrenal-region mass are real and recurring findings at this site. No morphology code is emitted and the case leaves the registry.

nodes.question: What exactly does the referral or clinical note say?
nodes.hint: A referral naming neuroblastoma, ganglioneuroblastoma, ganglioneuroma, paraganglioma or pheochromocytoma is not evidence that it is that entity — these are exactly the differential a referring clinician guesses between. None of this tree's six codes may be assigned without at least a biochemical marker and imaging together.
nodes.coding_note: Visser Rule 5 (p.03): everything without pathology is 8000/3, which is not a Group IV code at a Group IV topography — it routes to Group XII (build contract §4.2 point 3). A referral alone, with no imaging and no laboratory result in the file, does not even reach the imaging_pathway tier, so it refers out rather than falling back to a Group IV NOS.

options.label: The note names a specific tumour (neuroblastoma, ganglioneuroblastoma, ganglioneuroma, paraganglioma, or pheochromocytoma), but no imaging report and no laboratory result are in the file
options.reason: The referral names an entity, and it is recorded verbatim on the case, but it cannot be coded from a note alone: no imaging and no biochemical marker are in the file to support even the imaging-only route. Obtain the imaging report and the catecholamine or metanephrine work-up before this case can be coded.

options.label: The note describes a mass or a suspected tumour at this site without naming a specific entity, and no imaging report and no laboratory result are in the file
options.reason: Nothing beyond a clinical note is in the file. Obtain the imaging report and the catecholamine or metanephrine work-up before this case can be coded.

options.label: Further review of the file locates an imaging report or a laboratory result (urinary catecholamine metabolites, plasma or urinary metanephrines, or chromogranin A) not accounted for above

nodes.question: No tissue exists. Which biochemical work-up does the file describe?
nodes.hint: Only two entities in this tree can be coded from imaging and biochemistry alone, and each needs its own marker set: neuroblastoma needs urinary HVA and VMA; pheochromocytoma needs plasma or urinary metanephrines, or chromogranin A. Neither marker set substitutes for the other, and a case with neither documented cannot be coded here at all.
nodes.coding_note: Visser MJ et al. key-points summary Table 4 (p.06) names these as the ONLY two Group IV entities codeable with no pathology, both at ENCR basis 4. Rule 6 (p.05): basis 4 never stands alone — routed onward to the imaging_pathway node, which requires the imaging constellation AND the biochemistry together.

Plasma free metanephrines, 24-hour urinary fractionated metanephrines, or chromogranin A sent — a pheochromocytoma work-up
No biochemical marker was sent, or none of the above results are in the file

nodes.hint: ENCR Rule 5 (p.03): a malignancy without pathology and without one of the two Table 4 marker sets is coded 8000/3, which is not a code this group carries. The case is referred to Group XII pending further work-up.

diversion_criteria.reason: Ninety percent of neuroblastoma presents under age 5. An older child needs tissue to exclude other causes of a retroperitoneal or mediastinal mass rather than being coded on imaging and biochemistry alone.

diversion_criteria.reason: Atypical for neuroblastoma; favours a different adrenal or retroperitoneal lesion, and tissue is required.

diversion_criteria.reason: A biochemical picture overlapping with pheochromocytoma at the same site. Tissue is required to settle which entity is present rather than coding on the stronger-looking result alone.

diversion_criteria.reason: A biochemical picture overlapping with neuroblastoma at the same site. Tissue is required to settle which entity is present.

nodes.question: A specimen was obtained but is reported as inadequate, non-diagnostic, or crush artefact only. What is the plan?
nodes.hint: A non-diagnostic specimen cannot be coded to a Group IV entity: this group has no basis-1/2 route to a specific code, only the two Table 4 marker routes (basis 4) or tissue (basis 5, 7 or 8). Refer to Group XII rather than guessing a family.
nodes.coding_note: Visser Rule 5 (p.03): basis 1 or 2 means morphology 8000/3, except for entities in Table 3 — and ICCC-3 Group IV has no Table 3 entries at all. The Group 3 un_inadequate_specimen precedent (family NOS at basis 2) does NOT transfer here: Group III's forty-three Table 3 CNS rows permit exactly that, and Group IV's only no-pathology route is Table 4 (basis 4, and only for 9500/8700). So an inadequate specimen refers to Group XII (8000/3) rather than falling back to a Group IV code.

nodes.question: Only fine-needle aspiration or core-needle cytology exists — no excisional or incisional histology report is in the file. What does the cytology, with any immunocytochemistry performed, show?
nodes.hint: Cytology can support a family but cannot assess the Schwannian stroma architecture that separates neuroblastoma from ganglioneuroblastoma, nor the anatomic detail full histology gives. Code to the more general stem and say why.

options.label: Paraganglioma/pheochromocytoma pattern, with immunocytochemistry showing GATA3 positive
options.upgrade_path: An excisional or core biopsy would confirm the anatomic detail needed to assign the site-specific code (adrenal pheochromocytoma versus extra-adrenal sympathetic paraganglioma) and allow germline susceptibility gene testing.

options.label: Cytology is non-diagnostic, discordant, or immunocytochemistry was not performed

nodes.question: Tick each marker's result as the report states it.
nodes.hint: GATA3 is the marker that separates the paraganglioma/pheochromocytoma family from the neuroblastic family. PHOX2B, synaptophysin and chromogranin A are positive in BOTH families and do not by themselves separate them. Cytokeratin is negative in both — a positive result points away from this tree's differential entirely.
nodes.coding_note: Build contract §5.1, §10.1: PHOX2B does not separate neuroblastoma from pheochromocytoma/paraganglioma; both are PHOX2B positive (Ma Y et al., J Neuropathol Exp Neurol 2021;80(12):1108-16, for the neuroblastoma side; Manethova M et al., Virchows Arch 2023;482(4):679-86, for the paraganglioma side). Mete O et al. 2022 (pp.96-106) states the WHO paraganglioma/pheochromocytoma panel as INSM1, synaptophysin, chromogranin, keratins negative, then GATA3, tyrosine hydroxylase, dopamine beta-hydroxylase, choline acetyltransferase, with SOX10/S100 for sustentacular cells — PHOX2B is not on it. The first rule below routes an adrenal, cytokeratin-positive, GATA3-negative result to the adrenocortical carcinoma differential (ICCC-2017 subgroup XIa, ICD-O-3.2 8370/3, verified against ICCC-2017.sqlite groups.group_id 92), never to a code in this file.

resolution_logic.reason: Cytokeratin-positive and GATA3-negative in an adrenal mass points away from a neuroblastic or paraganglionic tumour of this group and towards adrenocortical carcinoma. Refer to Group XI and to the registrar to confirm cortical versus medullary origin.

nos_fallback.reason: Neither the paraganglioma/pheochromocytoma marker (GATA3 positive) nor the confirmatory neuroblastic panel (PHOX2B, synaptophysin and chromogranin A positive with GATA3 negative) was demonstrated. Coded to the tree's default, Neuroblastoma, NOS, pending a fuller immunohistochemical panel or expert pathology review.

nodes.question: The histology and immunohistochemistry confirm the paraganglioma/pheochromocytoma family. Where does the tumour arise?

Every site this tree owns outside the adrenal gland (peripheral nerve/autonomic nervous system, retroperitoneum, mediastinum) is a sympathetic-chain location, not a parasympathetic one — parasympathetic sites (carotid body, vagal, jugulotympanic) belong to a different tree entirely.

nodes.question: What does the histology report describe about ganglion cell differentiation and Schwannian stromal content?
nodes.hint: This is the International Neuroblastoma Pathology Committee (INPC) classification. Stroma-poor tissue composed of neuroblasts is neuroblastoma; stroma-rich tissue with ganglion cells intermixed throughout is ganglioneuroblastoma, intermixed; a distinct neuroblastic nodule within a ganglioneuroma or intermixed background is ganglioneuroblastoma, nodular; a uniformly mature, stroma-dominant tumour with no neuroblastic component anywhere is ganglioneuroma, which is benign and outside this group. Answer from what the report states, not from grade or differentiation detail the code does not need.
nodes.coding_note: Shimada 1999; Peuchmaur 2003 (INPC); Mete O et al. 2022 Table 1 (p.108), an independent second WHO-published reproduction of the same INPC classification (build contract §10.1); WHO Paediatric Tumours Supplementary Table S3 (Pfister 2022, per build contract table): Ganglioneuroma (maturing/mature) = 9490/0; Ganglioneuroblastoma, intermixed = 9490/3; Neuroblastoma (undifferentiated/poorly differentiated/differentiating) = 9500/3; Ganglioneuroblastoma, nodular (and other composite neuroblastic tumors) = 9490/3. Option D is the D1 behaviour_exclusion branch (build contract §2.1, §3, ratified registrar ruling D1); its wording requires the report to exclude BOTH a neuroblastic component AND a paraganglioma/pheochromocytoma component, so a composite case is directed to option E and can never reach the exclusion (build contract 'THE TRAP').

options.label: A single, uniform pattern throughout — Schwannian stroma-poor, composed of neuroblasts at any level of differentiation (undifferentiated, poorly differentiated, or differentiating) — with no ganglion cells and no Schwannian stroma-rich or mature component described anywhere

nodes.hint: Synaptophysin, chromogranin and INSM1 positive, pankeratin negative, S100/SOX10 on sustentacular cells only, is the Rooper 2023 panel for olfactory neuroblastoma. Calretinin positivity is the discriminator that separates it from other small round blue cell tumours of the sinonasal tract — use it. PHOX2B is not part of this panel: it is positive in only 1 of 6 olfactory neuroblastomas (Manethova M, et al. Virchows Arch 2023;482(4):679-86), so a negative PHOX2B does not exclude this diagnosis and must not be used to rule it out.

The vast majority of ONB are negative for pankeratin ... Classically, ONB is surrounded by a delicate network of sustentacular cells that are positive for S100 protein and SOX10. ONB is also consistently positive for calretinin, which can help differentiate it from overlapping small round blue cell tumors.' Agarwal A, et al., AJNR 2023;44(10):1116-1125, pp. 1122-23: 'malignant, neuroectodermal neoplasms' with 'diffuse staining for conventional neuroendocrine markers and S-100 protein'. Two entities proposed since the WHO 5th edition — olfactory carcinoma and IDH2-mutant sinonasal carcinoma — are carcinomas and belong to ICCC-3 Group XI, not Group IV; a keratin-positive sinonasal neuroectodermal tumour, especially with an intermixed glandular component, is the signal. nodes.question: Does the pathology or operative report state a Hyams grade and/or a Kadish or Kadish-Morita stage?

Five of the seven original Hyams criteria are subjective ordinal words with no count, percentage or area, and its own source paper found original Hyams grade not significantly associated with survival. Kadish defined three stages, A to C; Stage D is Morita's addition, so the four-stage system is properly called Kadish-Morita, not Kadish alone. Neither grade nor stage changes the ICD-O code: this tree's code is 9522/3 (or, on the report's own exact wording, 9520/3, 9521/3 or 9523/3) at every grade and every stage.

Rooper 2023: 'Tumor stage, as assessed by the Kadish-Morita system, is the most powerful predictor of outcomes in ONB, with Hyams grade having a smaller but definitive impact.' nodes.question: What does the report say about why the specimen did not yield a diagnosis?
nodes.hint: An inadequate specimen is not a negative one. The tissue was sought and an attempt was made to examine it, but it told nobody anything - there is no tissue diagnosis, so no Group IV code is emitted here.
nodes.coding_note: The shared terminus this tree's own entry option, and any sibling Group IV tree, routes to when a specimen was taken but did not yield a diagnosis. Group 3's un_inadequate_specimen precedent does NOT transfer here: Group 3 can emit its group NOS code at ENCR basis 2 because Visser Table 3 carries forty-three CNS rows permitting it. Group IV has no Table 3 entries, so Visser rule 5 (Front Oncol 2023;13:1250549, p. 03) governs instead - basis 2 with no tissue diagnosis is 8000/3, which is Group XII, not a Group IV code.

options.label: Too little tissue, or no lesional tissue was present in the specimen
options.reason: The specimen contained no diagnostic material. Under Visser rule 5 (Front Oncol 2023;13:1250549, p. 03), a case with no tissue diagnosis is coded 8000/3, Neoplasm, malignant, NOS, at ENCR basis 2 - and Group IV has no Table 3 entries permitting a specific morphology code at that basis. 8000/3 at this topography is not an ICCC-3 Group IV code. Code the case from the ICCC-3 Group XII tree until a repeat biopsy reaches lesional tissue.

provisional_pending.reason: The specimen contained no diagnostic material. A repeat biopsy that reaches lesional tissue is what resolves this and returns the case to this tree.

options.label: The section could not be read - crush artefact, failed processing, or no cells on the slide
options.reason: The preparation could not be interpreted, so no tissue diagnosis exists. Under Visser rule 5 (Front Oncol 2023;13:1250549, p. 03), that is coded 8000/3, Neoplasm, malignant, NOS, at ENCR basis 2, which is not an ICCC-3 Group IV code. Code the case from the ICCC-3 Group XII tree until the block is recut or a repeat biopsy yields a readable section.

provisional_pending.reason: Recutting the existing block, not necessarily a repeat operation, is what usually resolves an unreadable preparation. Either one returns the case to this tree.

nodes.question: Tissue was examined and reported somewhere. What can be established without that report?
nodes.hint: The basis of diagnosis is what this file can document, not what a laboratory once knew. With no report in the file there is no tissue diagnosis, and this group has no route that emits a specific code without one. Retrieving the report is the one step that changes that.
nodes.coding_note: Visser rule 5 (Front Oncol 2023;13:1250549, p. 03): a case with no tissue diagnosis in hand is 8000/3 at ENCR basis 2, and Group IV has no Table 3 entries permitting a specific code at that basis (unlike Group 3, which the un_report_missing precedent this node is modelled on can do). So neither option below emits a Group IV code.

options.label: The report exists and a copy can be requested
options.reason: Tissue was examined by someone and this file cannot see the result, so there is no tissue diagnosis in hand. Under Visser rule 5, that is 8000/3, Neoplasm, malignant, NOS - Group XII, not Group IV. Code the case from the ICCC-3 Group XII tree until the report is retrieved and the case can be reassessed against the entities this tree names.

provisional_pending.reason: The histology report exists and is not in the file. Retrieving it is what resolves this and returns the case to this tree.

options.label: The report cannot be retrieved - the laboratory has closed, the record is lost, or the specimen was sent abroad and never returned a result
options.reason: The tissue diagnosis is unrecoverable. Under Visser rule 5, no tissue diagnosis means 8000/3, Neoplasm, malignant, NOS - Group XII, not Group IV. Code the case from the ICCC-3 Group XII tree; this is the case's final code, not a provisional one.

options.label: The report has now been retrieved and names one of the entities this tree tracks

nodes.step_label: Medulloepithelioma family - coded on the report alone
nodes.question: What does the pathology report state about this medulloepithelioma-family tumour?
nodes.hint: There is no diagnostic pathway to run here. WHO's medulloepithelioma entity is described in the eye (retinal and neuroepithelial tumours); the WHO paediatric volume says nothing about a medulloepithelioma at this, a peripheral, non-ocular, non-CNS, site. Code exactly what the pathology report states, and record the topography with particular care - this is one of the rarest diagnoses this registry will ever see coded outside the eye.
nodes.coding_note: Pfister 2022 Supplementary Table S3 places medulloepithelioma under Retinal and neuroepithelial tumours, with benign/malignant and non-teratoid/teratoid subtypes, somatic DICER1 and KMT2D mutations, and germline DICER1. That is Group V, not Group IV. The only evidence held for a primary at a peripheral, non-ocular site is Shuangshoti S, et al., Br J Ophthalmol 1986;70(7):543-548, a single case report of a primary intraorbital extraocular tumour. No differential is built for 9501 or 9502 for this reason - the honest answer is that the diagnosis rests on the pathology report alone. The DICER1 link connects this stem to the ocular entity and is worth carrying forward if germline testing is ever done, but it is not a coding input.

This code is assigned on the pathology report alone; record the topography exactly as documented.

nodes.question: What exact wording does the pathology report use for this tumour?
nodes.hint: ICD-O-3.2 treats these wordings differently even though they describe similar-looking small round cell tumours. "Peripheral primitive neuroectodermal tumor", "peripheral neuroectodermal tumor" and "PPNET" are ICD-O-3.2's own synonyms for Ewing sarcoma. "Neuroepithelioma" and "peripheral neuroepithelioma" are not - the exact phrase "peripheral neuroepithelioma" does not appear anywhere in ICD-O-3.2, so what happens next is decided by the immunohistochemistry already in the file, not by the wording itself.
nodes.coding_note: D4 and D6. IARC's Summary of main changes: "Ewing sarcoma (9260/3) has moved to, and is now the preferred term for, 9364/3 (peripheral neuroectodermal tumour)." ICD-O-3.2 workbook, verified against both the 2019 draft and the 9 Oct 2020 final: 9364/3 Preferred Ewing sarcoma; Synonym Peripheral neuroectodermal tumor, PPNET; Related Peripheral primitive neuroectodermal tumor. 9503/3 Preferred Neuroepithelioma, NOS - and nothing else; no PNET synonym on this stem in either version. Alias-instruction entries 30, 31 and 33 (which sent this wording to 9503) are wrong and are overridden here; entry 29 (Neuroepithelioma alone, to 9503) stands, but every case in this family is still routed through the CD99/PHOX2B/synaptophysin check (op_ihc_cd99) rather than trusting the word, because that is the evidence-not-wording standard D6 sets and there is no reason to apply it selectively.

nodes.step_label: CD99 / PHOX2B / synaptophysin - Ewing-family or Neuroepithelioma, NOS
nodes.question: Is the tumour CD99 positive, with PHOX2B negative and synaptophysin negative?
nodes.hint: Answer from immunohistochemistry already in the file; do not order new testing to answer this question. "Peripheral neuroepithelioma" is not a defined pathology term - it appears nowhere in the ICD-O-3.2 workbook, under any code - so whether this tumour is coded Neuroepithelioma, NOS or referred out as an Ewing-family tumour is decided by the panel result already on file, not by which words the report happens to use.
nodes.coding_note: D6. CD99 positive with PHOX2B and synaptophysin both negative is the immunophenotype of the Ewing sarcoma family (9364/3), which ICD-O-3.2 states is what "peripheral (primitive) neuroectodermal tumor" and "PPNET" actually are (D4). Where the panel does not support that constellation, or was not done, 9503/3 Neuroepithelioma, NOS is the only ICD-O-3.2 stem this wording can carry - it has no other preferred term, in either the 2019 draft or the 9 Oct 2020 final workbook. 9364 must never be written to morphology_code anywhere in this tree; the Ewing-family branch is a refer_group terminal only, resolved at op_ewing_site.

marker_groups.group_label: Neuroblastic / neuroepithelial panel expected negative in Ewing family

resolution_logic.coding_note: CD99 positive, PHOX2B negative, synaptophysin negative: the Ewing-family immunophenotype. ICD-O-3.2 states this constellation's usual clinical name - peripheral (primitive) neuroectodermal tumor, PPNET - is Ewing sarcoma, 9364/3, not 9503.

resolution_logic.reason: CD99, PHOX2B and synaptophysin do not together support an Ewing-family tumour, or the panel was not done. 9503/3 Neuroepithelioma, NOS is the only ICD-O-3.2 stem this wording can carry. CD99, PHOX2B and synaptophysin remain an outstanding workup item on this case - a result that later completes the Ewing-family constellation replaces this code.

nos_fallback.reason: The CD99/PHOX2B/synaptophysin panel result was not recorded in a recognised state. The case falls to this tree's designated group-level code at the reportable behaviour; review before the record is closed. This is the tree's generic fallback, not a claim that the tumour is a neuroblastoma.

nodes.step_label: Ewing-family tumour - which registry tree completes the code
nodes.question: Where is the primary site of this tumour?
nodes.hint: This does not change the diagnosis - it decides which ICCC-3 group's tree carries the code, because Ewing sarcoma (9364/3) is a Group VIII code at a bony primary and a Group IX code at a soft-tissue primary, and neither is a Group IV code.
nodes.coding_note: 9364 must not appear as a morphology_code anywhere in this file; both options below are refer_group terminals only.

options.label: Bone
options.reason: CD99 positive, PHOX2B and synaptophysin negative (or the report's own wording already names Ewing sarcoma or a peripheral neuroectodermal tumour), at a bony primary site: an Ewing-family tumour, ICD-O-3.2 9364/3 Ewing sarcoma. Code this case from the ICCC-3 Group VIII (bone tumours) tree.

options.label: Soft tissue (extraosseous)
options.reason: CD99 positive, PHOX2B and synaptophysin negative (or the report's own wording already names Ewing sarcoma or a peripheral neuroectodermal tumour), at a soft-tissue, extraosseous primary site: an Ewing-family tumour, ICD-O-3.2 9364/3 Ewing sarcoma. Code this case from the ICCC-3 Group IX (soft tissue sarcomas) tree.

nodes.step_label: Paraganglioma-family tumour, site not covered by a dedicated tree
nodes.question: What does the pathology report establish about the primary site of this paraganglioma-family tumour?
nodes.hint: This tree carries only the generic paraganglioma stem. If the primary site can be matched to a carotid body, jugulotympanic, vagal, laryngeal, adrenal or sympathetic-chain location, a more specific code is available from this registry's dedicated head-and-neck or sympathoadrenal tree - check there first. Use this node only when the site genuinely does not match, or cannot be established at all.
nodes.coding_note: ICCC-2017 assigns 8680-8700 the full C00.0-C80.9 range (subgroup IVb), so a paraganglioma at an uncovered or unestablished site is still a Group IV case; it is coded to the generic stem because this tree has no site-specific differential to offer.

options.label: The primary site does not match any location this registry's dedicated paraganglioma trees cover
options.reason: The pathology confirms a paraganglioma-family tumour at a site outside the head-and-neck and sympathoadrenal trees' coverage. 8680/3 Paraganglioma, NOS is the generic stem this tree carries. Record the topography exactly as documented.

options.label: The primary site has not been established
options.reason: The pathology confirms a paraganglioma-family tumour, but the primary site could not be established. 8680/3 Paraganglioma, NOS is recorded with the topography documented as unknown primary; a specific stem can be assigned later if the primary is found.

captures.topography: C80.9 - unknown primary, if no other site is ever documented

nodes.step_label: Adequate tissue, no specific Group IV entity named
nodes.question: Tissue is adequate. What does the report establish?
nodes.hint: This is the tree's own group-level code, applied when tissue was examined and nothing above was named. It is a coded approximation, not a specific diagnosis - it does not assert the tumour is a classic neuroblastoma.
nodes.coding_note: 9500 is this tree's flat NOS fallback, exactly as 8000 is Group III's and 8680 is the paraganglionic trees' (contract section 4.4). Applying it to a genuinely unclassified peripheral neural/neuroendocrine tumour is the closest coded approximation ICD-O-3.2 offers in the absence of a named entity; it is not evidence that the tumour is neuroblastoma.

options.label: The report describes a small round blue cell, undifferentiated neuroendocrine, or peripheral neural tumour but names no specific entity
options.reason: Tissue was examined and shows a neural or neuroendocrine-type neoplasm, but no specific entity is named in the file. 9500/3 is this tree's designated group-level code, applied here as the closest coded approximation available; it does not assert this is a classic neuroblastoma. A later report naming a specific entity replaces this code.
